name: Dot object
shows: A real object rebuilt from dots. It is cut out of a photograph taken on a seamless plain ground (the ground, even a graded one, is modelled from the border; an object running off the edge is not taken for ground), or out of a cut-out PNG by its alpha. Each dot takes the photograph's tone where it sits, so the dots draw the form, not only the outline.
for: In the kit's gallery only, never on a page (references/effects-objects.md): no page prints, dithers or grades a photograph. What it was made for: a feature card about a real thing the product works with: a device the app runs or controls, the hardware a developer tool ships to, a product photographed for a shop builder or a photo app. Only with a plain-ground shot or a cut-out PNG; a busy or sunlit background does not cut out.
never: Never on a place, service, product or local-business page (a cafe, a shop, a hotel, a studio people visit, a maker of things): those show their photographs plain, or a product its object render, never printed in dots. No caption that explains the dots; the photograph's credit goes in the footer's one credit line.
motion: None at rest: the finished object, drawn once.
hover: A loupe: under the pointer the dots take the photograph's real colour and swell until they almost touch, so the object shows through the print; it eases back when the pointer leaves. Touch: the same under the finger.
reducedMotion: The same still object; the loupe follows the pointer without easing.

params.gap: CSS px between dots; default from the panel size, 4.2 to 7.5
params.fit: share of the panel the object fills, default 0.78
params.threshold: 0..1, how far from the ground colour counts as the object, default 0.5
params.radius: loupe radius in CSS px; default from the panel size, 70 to 150
params.focus: [x, y] crop centre of the fallback photograph

palette: ink dots on bg (dot size follows the photograph's darkness on a light page, its lightness on a dark one); under the loupe the photograph's own colours.
fallback: the photograph as an , cover-cropped at its focus.
cost: low: 3 000 to 8 000 points in a static buffer, one draw call, drawn only while the loupe moves
